newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Persetel buy cost nags market, shares fall.
newsitem.headline: Persetel buy cost nags market, shares fall.

text.p: Concerns that Persetel Holdings Ltd may have overpaid for its purchase of a controlling stake in German firm Telemation AG lopped over 1.5 percent off the value of the South African company's shares on Monday.
Dealers on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said profit-taking, after the share's recent strong rally following cautionary notices about a possible purchase, also weighed on the stock.

The information technology business said on Monday it was to buy a 70 percent controlling stake in Telemation for an undisclosed sum. Payment would be made through the issue of 70-million Persetel shares.
"Some people believe that the deal was done on a very high price/earnings ratio," one dealer said.
"Also once the news is out, there is usually some profit taking of sorts, especially as the shares have come a long way."
Persetel shares fell 65 cents or 1.66 percent to a morning low of 38.40 rand on Monday, toppling off Friday's record high close of 39.05.
Traders said shares could lose more ground, depending on the mood of the market.
"There is a Persetel presentation to analysts later today and if they can make a case to show that they did not overpay, the fall might be over," a dealer said.
Persetel shares have rocketed almost 400 percent since the beginning of last year, climbing from 775 cents to 38.50 rand at 1015 GMT on Monday.
Traders said the massive gains followed an 80 percent surge in Persetel's attributable income in the year to end May, 1996 and the acquisition of numerous data businesses during 1996.
The latest purchase lays to rest speculation following the release of two cautionary notices late last year.
